title: Eating out with friends
goal: Order for a group, choose Kathmandu street food, complain that something is too spicy or not salty enough, say what you're craving, and split the bill — or insist on paying.
intro:
Kathmandu eats out a lot: a plate of **मःम** at a hole-in-the-wall, **सेकुवा** and **छोयला** with friends in the evening, **चटपटे** and **पानीपुरी** from a street cart, **लाफिङ** in Boudha, and a **थाली** of dal-bhat that keeps getting refilled. This unit is about doing all that in Nepali.

You'll learn to say 'too / enough / a little' (**अति पिरो भयो**, **पुग्छ?**, **अलि कम**), how Nepalis say 'I feel like…' — including the wonderfully Nepali **खाऊँ खाऊँ लाग्यो** 'I'm dying to eat it' — and the 'each' forms you need for a group: **एक-एक प्लेट**, **आ-आफ्नो तिरौँ**.

grammar.title: Too, enough, a little
grammar.body:
**'Too…'**: Nepali usually says it with an adjective + **भयो** 'it has become' — the भयो itself suggests 'more than it should be': महँगो **भयो** 'it's (too) expensive', अलि नुनिलो **भयो** 'it's a bit too salty'. Add **धेरै**, **साह्रै** or the stronger **अति** for 'way too': **अति** पिरो भयो! 'far too spicy!'. Compare: पिरो **छ** 'it is spicy' (a fact) vs पिरो **भयो** 'it's (turned out) too spicy' (a complaint).

**'Enough'** is the verb **पुग्नु** 'to suffice' (the same verb as 'to arrive'): **पुग्छ** 'it's enough', **पुगेन** 'it wasn't enough', **पुग्यो!** 'that's enough, stop!'. Who it's enough for takes **लाई**: चार जना**लाई** पुग्छ? 'is it enough for four?'.

**'Not enough / less'**: **कम** — नुन **कम** भयो 'there isn't enough salt'; पिरो **कम** हाल्नुस् 'put less chilli'.

**'A little'**: **अलि** goes with adjectives (अलि पिरो 'a bit spicy', अलि कम 'a bit less'); **अलिकति** with things (अलिकति नुन 'a little salt'). **'More'**: **थप** 'extra, another helping' (अलिकति थप दिनुस्), **अझ** + adjective 'even more' (अझ पिरो).

examples.native: यो चिया त अति गुलियो भयो।
examples.roman: yo chiyā ta ati guliyo bhayo.
examples.en: This tea is far too sweet.
Are two plates enough for four people?
There wasn't enough rice — could we have a bit more?
The dal doesn't have enough salt.
Could you make it a little less spicy?

grammar.title: I feel like…: मन लाग्यो, खाऊँ खाऊँ लाग्यो
grammar.body:
Unit 17 taught **मलाई … -न मन छ / मन लाग्छ** 'I'd like to'. For food cravings Nepalis use it all the time, usually in the past form **लाग्यो** for a feeling that has just come over you:
**मलाई** सेकुवा **खान मन लाग्यो** 'I feel like sekuwa'.
The person feeling it takes **लाई** (मलाई, तिमीलाई, उसलाई), and the verb needs its **-न** form: खा**न**, पिउ**न**.

The really Nepali way to say 'I'm dying to…' doubles the 'shall I' form (**-ऊँ**, unit 18) and adds **लाग्नु**: **खाऊँ खाऊँ लाग्यो** 'I'm craving it (lit. 'shall I eat, shall I eat' it struck me)', **जाऊँ जाऊँ लाग्छ** 'I really want to go', **किनूँ किनूँ लाग्यो** 'I'm tempted to buy it'.

To ask: **के खान मन छ?** or **के खाने मन छ?** 'what do you feel like eating?'. To say no: **मन छैन** 'I don't feel like it', **मन लागेन** 'I didn't feel like it'.

Keep two things apart: **मलाई मःम मन पर्छ** 'I like momo' (in general) vs **मलाई मःम खान मन लाग्यो** 'I feel like momo (now)'.

examples.native: आज मलाई सेकुवा खान मन लाग्यो।
examples.roman: āja malāi sekuwā khāna man lāgyo.

examples.native: जाडोमा तातो झोल मःम खाऊँ खाऊँ लाग्छ।
examples.roman: jāḍomā tāto jhol momo khāuṃ khāuṃ lāgchha.
examples.en: In winter you just crave hot jhol momo.

examples.roman: malāi āja bāhira khāna man chhaina.
examples.en: I don't feel like eating out today.

examples.native: मलाई मःम मन पर्छ, तर अहिले चाउमिन खान मन लाग्यो।
examples.roman: malāi momo man parchha, tara ahile chāumin khāna man lāgyo.
examples.en: I like momo, but right now I feel like chow mein.

grammar.title: One each, each their own: एक-एक, आ-आफ्नो, के-के
grammar.body:
Doubling a word is a key Nepali tool, and at a group meal it's everywhere:

**Number + same number = 'each'**: **एक-एक** प्लेट 'a plate each', **दुई-दुईवटा** 'two each', **सय-सय** रुपैयाँ 'a hundred rupees each', **पाँच-पाँच सय** 'five hundred each'.

**आ-आफ्नो** 'each their own' (from आफ्नो 'one's own'): **आ-आफ्नो** तिरौँ 'let's each pay for our own', **आ-आफ्नो** अर्डर गर 'everyone order for yourself'.

**Question word doubled = 'which all / what all'** — it asks for a list: **के-के** अर्डर गर्ने? 'what (all) shall we order?', **को-को** आउँदै छन्? 'who (all) is coming?', **कहाँ-कहाँ** गयौ? 'where all did you go?'.

For numbers of people use **जना**: पाँच **जना**को लागि टेबल 'a table for five'.

examples.native: बिल चार सय भयो, सय-सय तिरौँ।
examples.roman: bil chār saya bhayo, saya-saya tirauṃ.
examples.en: The bill's four hundred — let's pay a hundred each.
Let's each pay our own today, OK?
Have you got a table for five?

dialogue.title: Sekuwa night
dialogue.setting: Anil, Rojina, Suman and Priya meet at a busy sekuwa place in Kathmandu on a Friday evening.

lines.speaker: Anil
lines.en: Could we have the menu, please?

lines.speaker: Rojina
lines.native: मेनु पर्दैन, यहाँको सेकुवा नै सबैभन्दा मिठो।
lines.roman: menu pardaina, yahāṃko sekuwā nai sabaibhandā miṭho.
lines.en: No need for the menu — the sekuwa here is the best thing.

lines.speaker: Suman
lines.native: मलाई त आज झोल मःम खाऊँ खाऊँ लागेको छ।
lines.roman: malāi ta āja jhol momo khāuṃ khāuṃ lāgeko chha.
lines.en: I'm dying for jhol momo today.

lines.speaker: Anil
lines.native: लौ, दुवै अर्डर गरौँ। के-के खाने?
lines.roman: lau, duwai arḍar garauṃ. ke-ke khāne?
lines.en: Fine, let's order both. What else shall we get?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: दुई प्लेट सेकुवा, दुई प्लेट झोल मःम, अनि एउटा चटपटे। चार जनालाई पुग्छ?
lines.roman: dui pleṭ sekuwā, dui pleṭ jhol momo, ani euṭā chaṭpaṭe. chār janālāi pugchha?
lines.en: Two plates of sekuwa, two of jhol momo, and a chatpate. Is that enough for four?

lines.speaker: Anil
lines.native: पुग्छ पुग्छ। दाइ, सेकुवा अलि कम पिरो बनाइदिनुस् है, प्रियालाई पिरो चल्दैन।
lines.roman: pugchha pugchha. dāi, sekuwā ali kam piro banāidinus hai, Priyālāi piro chaldaina.
lines.en: Plenty. Could you make the sekuwa a bit less spicy? Priya can't handle chilli.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: हो, पोहोर यहाँको अचार खाएर म रोएँ!
lines.roman: ho, pohor yahāṃko achār khāera ma roeṃ!
lines.en: True — last year I ate the pickle here and cried!

lines.speaker: Suman
lines.native: वाह, कस्तो मिठो! तर झोल अलि नुनिलो भयो।
lines.roman: wāh, kasto miṭho! tara jhol ali nunilo bhayo.
lines.en: Wow, so good! The soup is a bit salty, though.

lines.speaker: Rojina
lines.native: खाना सेलाउनुअघि खाऊ, गफ पछि गर्नू!
lines.roman: khānā selāunuaghi khāu, gaph pachhi garnu!
lines.en: Eat before it gets cold — chat later!

lines.speaker: Anil
lines.native: म त अघाएँ। दाइ, हिसाब गरिदिनुस्।
lines.roman: ma ta aghāeṃ. dāi, hisāb garidinus.
lines.en: I'm stuffed. Could we have the bill, please?

lines.speaker: Suman
lines.native: आज मेरो तर्फबाट ट्रिट! मेरो जागिर पक्का भयो।
lines.roman: āja mero tarphabāṭa ṭriṭ! mero jāgir pakkā bhayo.
lines.en: Tonight's on me! I got the job.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: साँच्चै? बधाई छ! तर बिल त ठूलो छ नि, आधा-आधा गरौँ न।
lines.roman: sāṃchchai? badhāi chha! tara bil ta ṭhulo chha ni, ādhā-ādhā garauṃ na.
lines.en: Really? Congratulations! But the bill's big — let's at least go halves.

lines.speaker: Suman
lines.native: पर्दैन, आज म तिर्छु। अर्को पटक तिमीहरूको पालो!
lines.roman: pardaina, āja ma tirchhu. arko paṭak timiharuko pālo!
lines.en: No need, I'm paying tonight. Next time it's your turn!

culture: Momo are everywhere in Kathmandu — steamed, fried (**तारेको**), in soup (**झोल**) or with chilli sauce (*C-momo*) — and the default filling is **बफ** (buffalo); ask for चिकेन or **भेज** (veg) if you prefer. In the evening friends go for **सेकुवा** or to a Newari **खाजाघर** for **छोयला**, **बारा** and **समय बजी**; in Boudha it's **लाफिङ**. At a dal-bhat place the server comes round with more rice and dal — say **पुग्यो** firmly (and cover your plate) when you're done, or it will keep coming. Call staff **दाइ**, **भाइ**, **दिदी** or **बहिनी**, never 'waiter'. Plates are shared and ordered together (**के-के खाने?**). Traditionally one person pays, and there's a good-natured fight over the bill; a new job, a passed exam or a birthday means you owe your friends a **ट्रिट**. Students and young professionals increasingly split (**आ-आफ्नो**), which is fine to suggest. Eat dal-bhat with your **right hand**, and don't offer anyone food from your own plate once you've started — it has become **जुठो** (ritually 'used').

lessons.title: Ordering for the group

tip.title: One each: एक-एक, के-के
tip.body:
- Double a number for 'each': **एक-एक** प्लेट 'a plate each', **दुई-दुई**वटा 'two each'.
- Double a question word for a list: **के-के** अर्डर गर्ने? 'what all shall we order?'
- **आ-आफ्नो** = 'each their own'.
- People: पाँच **जना**.

new: हामी सबैलाई एक-एक प्लेट बफ मःम दिनुस्।

A thali for everyone, please.

tip.title: Fried, grilled, in soup
tip.body:
- Cooking words are **-एको** forms used as adjectives (unit 20): **तारेको** 'fried', **पोलेको** 'grilled', **उमालेको** 'boiled'.
- They go before the noun: **तारेको** मःम.
- **झोल** 'soup, broth': **झोल** मःम.

sentences.roman: ma tāreko momo khānchhu, timi ni?
sentences.en: I'll have fried momo — what about you?
Grilled chicken is tasty.
You get good laphing in Boudha.
Make the chatpate a bit spicy, please.
Jhol momo or fried?

sentences.roman: chhoylā ali piro hunchha, khāera hera.
sentences.en: Choila's a bit spicy — give it a try.

sentences.native: सेकुवा र चाउमिन, दुवै अर्डर गरौँ।
sentences.roman: sekuwā ra chāumin, duwai arḍar garauṃ.
sentences.en: Let's order both the sekuwa and the chow mein.
Let's have chow mein for a snack.

tip.title: Too, enough, a little
tip.body:
- 'Too…' = adjective + **भयो**: नुनिलो **भयो**. Stronger: **अति** पिरो भयो!
- 'Enough' = **पुग्नु**: **पुग्छ**? · **पुगेन** · **पुग्यो!** 'stop!'
- 'Not enough / less' = **कम**: नुन **कम** भयो.
- 'A bit' = **अलि** + adjective, **अलिकति** + thing.

sentences.en: The momo pickle is way too spicy.

sentences.native: तरकारी अलि खल्लो भयो, नुन दिनुस् त।
sentences.roman: tarkāri ali khallo bhayo, nun dinus ta.
sentences.en: The curry's a bit bland — could I have some salt?
The chow mein is too salty.
Are two plates enough for three people?
That tea wasn't enough — another one, please.

sentences.native: मसला अलि कम हालिदिनुस्, धेरै पिरो खान सक्दिनँ।
sentences.roman: masalā ali kam hālidinus, dherai piro khāna sakdinaṃ.
sentences.en: Go easy on the spices please — I can't eat very spicy food.
It tastes a bit sour.
You put far too much sugar in.
That's enough, that's plenty now!

tip.title: I feel like…
tip.body:
- **मलाई** + verb-**न** + **मन लाग्यो** = 'I feel like (now)': मलाई चिया पिउ**न मन लाग्यो**.
- Dying for it: double the -ऊँ form: **खाऊँ खाऊँ लाग्यो**.
- Ask: **के खान मन छ?** No: **मन छैन**.
- Not the same as **मन पर्छ** 'I like (in general)'.
tip.pattern: मलाई + verb-न + मन लाग्यो  ·  खाऊँ खाऊँ लाग्यो

tip.title: Treating and splitting
tip.body:
- Often one person pays: **आज मेरो तर्फबाट ट्रिट!** Expect a friendly fight over it.
- Good news means you owe a treat: **ट्रिट कहिले दिने?**
- Splitting: **आधा-आधा गरौँ**, **आ-आफ्नो तिरौँ**, **पाँच-पाँच सय**.
- Ask for the bill: **दाइ, हिसाब गरिदिनुस्**.

sentences.en: You paid yesterday, today I'll pay.
